results.title: Wavefront: Low-Rank Drafting with Parallel Causal Refinement for Speculative Decoding
results.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by letting a cheap drafter propose tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Parallel block drafters such as DFlash and P-EAGLE propose a whole block in one forward pass, but they lose the dependence between tokens in the block; DSpark restores part of it with a lightweight correction head that runs sequentially. Measuring DSpark, we find that this head overrides the base prediction on most slots, so the expensive base readout through the target's full lm_head mostly provides a seed. We therefore propose Wavefront, which follows a simple principle: shrink the base and strengthen the correction head. Wavefront replaces the full lm_head with a learned low-rank base, conditions the correction head on the whole drafted prefix within the same block, and resolves it with a few parallel Jacobi passes. A fixed pass budget makes the draft step free of data-dependent control flow, so we capture it as a single CUDA graph in vLLM with fused kernels. On Qwen3-8B, Wavefront improves throughput over xPress, DSpark and DFlash by 2.6%, 10.7% and 23.6% on average across math, code, chat and agentic benchmarks, and by 9.6%, 14.3% and 28.9% on SPEED-Bench long-context prompts. On Qwen3.8-27B it leads DFlash2, DSpark and xPress by 7.6%, 10.6% and 5.0%, and by 7.4%, 5.8% and 6.0% on the same long-context prompts. The gains persist as serving load grows to concurrency 32.

results.title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
results.abstract: Sustained Large Language Model (LLM) inference generates significant heat that exacerbates silicon aging and reduces GPU reliability. Because GPU temperature fluctuates continuously with workload intensity and ambient conditions, keeping it in a safe range requires real-time frequency scaling, which inevitably comes at the cost of either throughput or accuracy. To address this tightly coupled challenge, we propose GreenDynaMix, the first runtime system to jointly integrate a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator. A sensitivity-aware allocator leverages intrinsic importance signals from the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router to assign higher precision to critical experts, preserving accuracy. Experiments on server, desktop, and embedded platforms demonstrate that GreenDynaMix reduces the temperature-induced aging rate of GPUs during LLM inference by 25-33%. Without offline profiling or model retraining, it recovers throughput at a perplexity cost of 0.9-1.6% with 8-bit/4-bit mixed precision, rising to 9.4% where memory forces 4-bit/2-bit.
